problem_markdown: For $1\le r\le n$, take every $r$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Show that the average of their minimum elements is $(n+1)/(r+1)$.
solutions_markdown:
The sum of all minima counts pairs $(S,t)$ where $S$ is an $r$-element subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $1\le t\le\min S$. Map this pair to the $(r+1)$-element subset
$$\{t\}\cup\{s+1:s\in S\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n+1\}.$$
Its least member is $t$, so the map is bijective: remove the least member and subtract one from all others. Thus the sum of minima is $\binom{n+1}{r+1}$. Dividing by the number $\binom nr$ of subsets gives the stated average.
